context.description: Kangaroo Island lies off South Australia's Fleurieu Peninsula, with Kingscote as its main town and the ferry reaching Penneshaw. Flinders Chase National Park fills the wild west, while the south coast has sea lion beaches, caves and dunes and the north coast has sheltered bays. Wildlife is the draw, from Australian sea lions and long-nosed fur seals to kangaroos and koalas. Distances are long, so most visitors base in Kingscote, Penneshaw or American River and drive out.

context.description: Mount Gambier is the second most populated city in South Australia, built on the slopes of a dormant volcano about 450 km south-east of Adelaide and 17 km from the Victorian border. The Blue Lake and Valley Lake fill volcanic craters on its southern edge, while sinkholes open inside the city at the Cave Garden and Umpherston Sinkhole. Beyond town, Mount Schank's crater rim, the spring-fed ponds at Ewens and Piccaninnie, and the show cave at Tantanoola are day trips. Port MacDonnell, on the coast to the south, has the Cape Northumberland headland.

context.description: Robe is a coastal town on Guichen Bay on the Limestone Coast, about 340 km from Adelaide. Founded in 1846, it became South Australia's second-busiest port in the 1850s, and more than 16,000 Chinese gold seekers landed here and walked about 320 km to the Victorian goldfields. That past survives in its 1863 customs house and the cliff-top obelisk, while Long Beach and Little Dip Conservation Park cover surf, dunes and lakes to the south. Rock lobster is a mainstay of the local fishing industry.

context.description: Beachport is a small town on Rivoli Bay on the Limestone Coast, about 385 km from Adelaide. An 1879 wool and grain store beside the old railway line is now a National Trust museum, and a long jetty reaches out over the bay. Around the town, a salt lake for floating, limestone cliffs in Beachport Conservation Park and the surf beaches and dunes of Canunda National Park fill a day or two.
